content-block-2:
Understanding Ultrasound for Pets

Ultrasound is a non-invasive diagnostic imaging technique that allows our veterinary team to visualize your pet’s internal organs in real time.

It is painless, does not expose pets to radiation, and provides detailed information that is often not available through x-rays or physical examinations alone.

Using ultrasound, we can assess the abdomen, monitor pregnancies, guide fine needle aspirates, and examine specific organs such as the liver, spleen, kidneys, and bladder.

This technology helps us quickly detect abnormalities, monitor chronic conditions, or rule out health concerns.

Having a board-certified internal medicine specialist like Dr. Armstrong perform your pet’s ultrasound in Miami-Dade and Monroe counties ensures thorough evaluation and interpretation.

At The Veterinary Internal Medicine Group, we are committed to providing top-tier diagnostic care, helping you make informed decisions while minimizing stress for your pet.

Serving Miami-Dade and Monroe counties and surrounding communities, we focus on delivering immediate results, answers, and personal attention at every ultrasound appointment.

content-block-3:
Why Ultrasound is Important for Your Pet

Veterinary ultrasound in Miami-Dade and Monroe counties is a key diagnostic tool for uncovering internal health issues early and accurately.

It is essential for evaluating unexplained symptoms, confirming diagnoses, monitoring treatment progress, and detecting hidden concerns.

Abdominal ultrasounds can identify tumors, organ disease, inflammation, bladder stones, or gastrointestinal problems before they progress.

For breeding animals, ultrasound provides a safe method for pregnancy checks with immediate, reliable results.

Early detection leads to more effective, less invasive treatments and improves your pet’s prognosis across a wide range of medical conditions.

Accurate, Early Diagnosis

Ultrasound enables our veterinary team to detect internal abnormalities with greater precision and earlier than many other modalities.

Timely diagnosis allows for more successful intervention.

Minimally Invasive and Stress-Free

This imaging is non-invasive, does not require surgery or sedation in most cases, and causes minimal discomfort.

Our approach, centered around keeping you present, further reduces stress for your pet.

Improves Treatment Outcomes

The clarity and detail from ultrasound help tailor your pet's treatment plan, supporting faster recovery and better long-term outcomes.

It is critical for managing chronic diseases or monitoring changes over time.

Signs Your Pet May Need an Ultrasound

Knowing when to seek pet ultrasound services in Miami-Dade and Monroe counties is vital for your pet’s health.

Some dogs or cats show subtle symptoms that require advanced imaging for answers.

  • Loss of appetite or unexplained weight loss
  • Vomiting or persistent diarrhea
  • Abdominal pain, swelling, or discomfort
  • Changes in urination or straining to urinate
  • Unexplained lethargy, weakness, or fainting

If you notice any of these signs, contact The Veterinary Internal Medicine Group promptly for an evaluation.

Timely veterinary ultrasounds can provide crucial answers and may lead to more positive outcomes for your pet.

How Often Should Your Pet Receive Ultrasound Exams?

The frequency of pet ultrasounds depends on your pet’s age, medical history, and current health concerns.

For ongoing management of chronic diseases, more frequent scans may be recommended, while healthy pets may only need ultrasounds when specific concerns arise.

Breeds with predisposing risks, pets undergoing pregnancy, or those experiencing unexplained symptoms should receive an ultrasound as soon as an issue is detected.

Dr. Armstrong and our veterinary professionals will recommend a personalized ultrasound schedule as part of a complete internal medicine approach.

Rely on our expertise to advise the right diagnostic interval to best support your pet’s wellbeing.
